finding.claim: The /rss endpoint passes the user-supplied `u` parameter straight to URI.open, with no validation. An attacker can make the server fetch any URL, including internal hosts, cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254, and localhost services. The first 400 bytes of the response are returned to the attacker, so this is a non-blind SSRF. Because open-uri is loaded, redirects are also followed. On older Ruby versions, Kernel#open semantics may add more risk, but URI.open itself is enough here.

trace.note: params[:u] is passed directly to URI.open, and the body is read
The first 400 bytes of the fetched response are returned to the client

finding.guards_checked: No scheme check, host allowlist, or private/loopback IP block. The TRUSTED allowlist is not applied on this route. No redirect restrictions.

verdict.reason: app.rb:8 passes unvalidated params[:u] from the GET /rss handler (app.rb:7) to URI.open(...).read, and app.rb:9 returns the first 400 bytes. The TRUSTED allowlist is only applied in the separate /trusted route (app.rb:14), and there is no middleware or other guard.
